subject: [Escalation] Customer latency surge tied to quota gating behaviour
messages:
From: Tim Jensen <tim.jensen@acuityrx.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Spike in latency & 5xxs during our promo window (urgent)

Laura —

We saw sustained 500/502 spikes and token-level latency jumping to 3–4s per token between 08:30–09:15 PST during our high-volume campaign this morning. This started after you rolled the revised burst window last week. The symptoms: stalled responses, partial completions and some dropped requests. Our revenue impact estimate for the hour is ~$12k in lost orders.

Can you confirm whether any quota/burst changes on your side could have caused this? We need a hotfix and a timeline for a rollback if necessary.

Attaching logs and a short sample of failure traces.

—Tim
Tim Jensen
Head of Platform Engineering, AcuityRx
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Tim Jensen <tim.jensen@acuityrx.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Feb 2027 09:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Spike in latency & 5xxs during our promo window (urgent)

Tim —

Thank you for the quick heads-up and for the logs. I’ve looped in Karthik and Neha from runtime/ops and Markus from account success. We’re treating this as P1.

Immediate asks:
- Karthik: can you confirm whether the new per-tenant burst gate and quota-window patch shipped Wednesday could interact with AcuityRx’s tenancy to force abrupt request curtailment?
- Neha: please pull the tenant-level metrics (qps, bucket tokens, burst credits) and share an annotated timeline.

Tim — we’ll send an update within 60 minutes with either a mitigation or a rollback plan.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Director, Enterprise Success — Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Feb 2027 10:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Spike in latency & 5xxs during our promo window (urgent)

Quick summary from runtime: we rolled a change to burst-window alignment on 2027-02-10 that tightened the bucket refill cadence for long-lived tenants to reduce cross-tenant noise. That change inadvertently interacts with long-tail seq distributions for tenants that sustain steady high QPS with short bursts.

Preliminary findings for AcuityRx:
- Their request profile keeps a shallow but steady prefix cache hit rate; when traffic spikes, the quota gating consumes burst credits quickly and then the safety valve clamps throughput to the baseline window (not a graceful degrade).
- The effect is sudden head-of-line latency increases and a sharp rise in 5xx when requests time out waiting for available tokens.

Immediate mitigation I can push now:
1) Relax the per-tenant burst clamp for AcuityRx (temporary override) — should restore serving within ~2 mins and avoid hard denials.
2) If override is insufficient, rollback the window-tightening change (30–45 min to validate & fully rollback).

I’ll push the override and report back. Also attaching a diff of the config and a small script to reproduce locally.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Staff Engineer, Runtime
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Feb 2027 10:29:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Spike in latency & 5xxs during our promo window (urgent)

Timeline (annotated):
- 08:27 PST — Ascent in inbound QPS from 420→1,950 sustained for ~18 minutes (campaign spike).
- 08:33 PST — KV cache hit fraction drops ~12% as new long-tail prompts arrive.
- 08:34 PST — Burst credit pool for tenant exhausted; gating transitioned to baseline window at 08:34:12.
- 08:34–08:43 PST — Error rate climbs from 0.4%→6.2%, median token latency rises from 200ms→1.8s.
- 08:47 PST — Karthik pushed temporary override; metrics show error rate falling back to 0.6% by 08:50 PST.

Attachments: SLA-traffic-logs-20270214-20270216.zip (samples), quota-config-diff-20270215.txt (shows the tighter window config).

Notes: override succeeded and customer reports partial recovery, but we should follow with a root-cause remediation and an exec note for the customer (they’ve already flagged this to procurement).

—Neha
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Tim Jensen <tim.jensen@acuityrx.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Procurement <procurement@acuityrx.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Feb 2027 17:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Spike in latency & 5xxs during our promo window (urgent)

Tim — thanks again for patience while we investigated. Short update and next steps:

What happened: a recent change to per-tenant burst-window alignment reduced refill granularity for long-running tenants. Under AcuityRx’s bursty campaign load this caused burst credits to be exhausted quickly and the safety valve to clamp traffic abruptly rather than gracefully degrade. That produced the observed latency and 5xx spike.

What we did immediately:
- Karthik applied a temporary per-tenant override (restored normal flow within minutes).
- We rolled a targeted rollback for the window-tightening change for AcuityRx and two other high-frequency tenants as a precaution.
- We provided AcuityRx with the logs and a timeline (attached and shared via Drive).

Committed remediation:
- Engineering will introduce a smoother degradation path (gradual pacing fallback) before global policy changes are rolled.
- A canary + synthetic-test step will be added to the rollout playbook for any burst/quotawindow changes that affect long-lived tenants.
- We will run a tenant-impact audit for the next 60 days and send weekly progress reports.

Customer-facing asks:
- Markus, we need an exec note summarising impact and confirmation of credits/waiver for the affected hour. Recommendation: 1 hour of usage credits + priority support voucher.
- Procurement (AcuityRx): please confirm a single POC for financial reconciliation.

Tim, we understand the disruption this caused and will follow up with a short exec summary (<2 pages) by EOD tomorrow and a roadmap for the remediation milestones.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Director, Enterprise Success — Redwood Inference
